the hydrogen-bonded lysine pair in the human transferrin N-lobe is important for iron release, but that the lysine residues are not the proton donor to the iron ligand tyrosine, and that the lysine pair is more flexible than previously thought.

the dilysine residues in transferrin, Lys206/Lys296, have a role in iron release but not by creating repulsive electrostatic forces as previously thought, and the dilysine pairs in transferrin have a role in the weakening of the iron binding by the tyrosine residue, Tyr188, as a step in the release of iron.
a hydrogen-bonding network involving two lysine side chains, Lys206 (N-lobe) and Lys296 (C-lobe), is important for iron release from the N-lobe site of human serum transferrin.

the role of the dilysines in iron release.
the structure and function of the protein, human transferrin (hTF), a serum protein that transports iron in the body and delivers it to cells.
the molecular basis of iron transport by transferrin and the role of the dilysines in iron release.

the dilysine motif of Tf is flexible and can be manipulated to alter its function in iron release.
